title: Longest Balanced Subarray II
summary: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest subarray where the count of distinct even numbers matches the count of distinct odd numbers.
statement: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest subarray where the count of distinct even numbers matches the count of distinct odd numbers.
constraints: nums contains up to 100,000 positive integers.
Balance compares counts of distinct even and distinct odd values in a contiguous subarray.
Return the maximum balanced subarray length.
hints: For every possible left boundary, maintain distinct odd-minus-even count for the current right endpoint.
When a value repeats, remove its old contribution from all earlier eligible left boundaries, then add its new contribution to later boundaries.
A lazy segment tree range-adds those changes and finds the earliest boundary with the current prefix balance.
Equal balances mean the intervening subarray has net distinct-parity count zero; choosing the earliest boundary maximizes its length.
editorial: Equal balances mean the intervening subarray has net distinct-parity count zero; choosing the earliest boundary maximizes its length.

tests.explanation: The full array has two distinct values of each parity, so its length is four.
The full array has two distinct odd and two distinct even values, so its length is five.
